title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (Act No. 23 of 1940 - Chapter IV-A)
authority: Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) / Ministry of Ayush
issuing_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / Ministry of Ayush

provisions.heading: Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani Drug
provisions.text: 'Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug' includes all medicines intended for internal or external use for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of disease or disorder in human beings or animals, and manufactured exclusively in accordance with the formulae described in the authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani systems of medicine specified in the First Schedule.
provisions.statutory_significance: Legal foundation of Classical (Shastriya) Ayurvedic medicines.

provisions.heading: Definition of Drug
provisions.text: “drug” includes— (i) all medicines for internal or external use of human beings or animals and all substances intended to be used for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of any disease or disorder in human beings or animals, including preparations applied on human body for the purpose of repelling insects like mosquitoes; (ii) such substances (other than food) intended to affect the structure or any function of the human body or intended to be used for the destruction of vermin or insects which cause disease in human beings or animals, as may be specified from time to time by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette; (iii) all substances intended for use as components of a drug including empty gelatin capsules; and (iv) such devices intended for internal or external use in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of disease or disorder in human beings or animals.
provisions.statutory_significance: Distinguishes medicines and therapeutic topical formulations from cosmetics; formulations with disease mitigation claims fall under Section 3(b).

provisions.heading: Patent or Proprietary Medicine in Relation to ASU
provisions.text: 'patent or proprietary medicine', in relation to Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani systems of medicine, means a drug which is a remedy or prescription presented in a form ready for internal or external administration on or in human beings or animals and which is not included in the authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani systems of medicine specified in the First Schedule.
provisions.statutory_significance: Legal definition for non-classical Ayurvedic formulations requiring safety/efficacy validation.

provisions.heading: Misbranded ASU Drugs
provisions.text: For the purposes of this Chapter, an Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug shall be deemed to be misbranded if it is so coloured, coated, powdered or polished that damage is concealed, or if it is not labelled in the prescribed manner, or if its label makes false claims regarding curative or therapeutic properties.

location.chapter: Chapter IV-A (Provisions Relating to ASU Drugs)

provisions.statutory_significance: Statutory offence for unauthorized therapeutic claims on ASU packaging.

provisions.heading: Standards to be Complied with by Imported Drugs and by Drugs Manufactured for Sale, Sold, Stocked or Exhibited for Sale, or Distributed
provisions.text: For Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs, the standard of quality is the standards set forth in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API), Siddha Pharmacopoeia, or Unani Pharmacopoeia for the time being in force.
provisions.statutory_significance: Mandatory statutory benchmark for raw material and finished product monograph standards.
